summary: Bradbury is one of the smallest incorporated cities in Los Angeles County — fewer than 900 residents spread across two square miles of foothill terrain at the base of the San Gabriel Mountains, where the landscape tilts upward toward chaparral ridgelines and the lots are measured in acres, not square feet. There are no sidewalks in most of the city, no commercial district, and essentially no retail or dining; this is a place defined by what it chose not to build. The median home value exceeds $1.9 million against a median household income of roughly $159,000, producing a home-value-to-income ratio above 12:1 — meaning even at the local median income, purchasing here requires substantial existing wealth or assets beyond salary. Employment is entirely elsewhere; Bradbury functions as a bedroom community whose residents commute into greater Pasadena, downtown Los Angeles, or the broader San Gabriel Valley, typically via the 210 freeway at its doorstep. The climate is textbook inland Southern California — 9.4 hours of daily sunshine, mid-70s highs, mild winters — and proximity to trails in the Angeles National Forest puts serious hiking minutes from home. Violent crime registered at zero across all categories, though property crime, overwhelmingly burglary, runs notably high per capita at over 1,200 per 100,000. Bradbury is less a town than a zoning philosophy: maximum space, minimum infrastructure, with every convenience requiring a car to reach.
